profile.reading:
This is one of three data center buildings on Vantage Data Centers' New Albany, Ohio campus at 3325 Horizon Court, in the New Albany International Business Park spanning Licking and Franklin counties, now one of the largest concentrations of hyperscale data center construction in the eastern United States. The park has drawn Amazon Web Services, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Vantage, attracted by AEP Ohio's transmission capacity, Ohio's data center sales and use tax exemption program, and local economic development incentive agreements negotiated with New Albany and Licking County.

Vantage's own campus materials describe the site as roughly 70 acres with about 1.5 million square feet planned across three two story buildings, each stated at approximately 64 megawatts of critical IT capacity, for a total campus capacity near 192 megawatts once fully built out. Vantage's page does not assign individual names, building numbers, or separately confirmed square footage figures to each of the three structures beyond this uniform per building description, so an even division of the 1.5 million total, approximately 500,000 square feet per building, is this profile's derived estimate rather than an operator confirmed figure for this specific building. Vantage has stated the first of the three buildings was slated to reach operational status in December 2025, with additional phases continuing through 2028. Power is supplied end to end at 480 volts, with N+1 electrical and N+2 mechanical redundancy per Vantage's standard design approach, and each building is targeted for LEED Silver certification.

Vantage's own company overview describes the New Albany project as an investment of more than 2 billion dollars and frames it as the company's entry into the Midwest United States market. Vantage Data Centers was founded in June 2010 with an investment from Silver Lake Partners and began by acquiring a former Intel data center in Santa Clara, California, before DigitalBridge became its majority owner in 2017. By its own current account the company operates more than 18 locations across North America, more than 15 across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, and more than 9 across Asia Pacific. In 2024 its owners DigitalBridge and Silver Lake completed a 9.2 billion dollar equity investment in Vantage, later upsized by a further 2.8 billion dollars, to support global hyperscale customer demand, according to the company's own materials.

Ohio's rapid data center buildout, concentrated heavily in New Albany and neighboring Licking County communities, has become a subject of statewide debate over electricity rate impacts on residential ratepayers, prompting AEP Ohio to propose a distinct large load tariff classification for data centers before the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio.

reading.body:
Vantage Building 2 is one of three structures in construction at Vantage's New Albany campus in Ohio, designed by the operator at 64 megawatts of critical IT capacity per building. The full campus is planned at 192 megawatts total across approximately 1.5 million square feet, with phased completion through 2028. The first building was targeted for December 2025, though this has not been confirmed as delivered.

At 64 megawatts of IT load, this single building would house roughly 1,600 racks at a common AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, though Vantage's actual mix of workloads and power densities are not published. The building is certified for LEED Silver and designed with N+1 electrical and N+2 mechanical redundancy at 480 volts. It qualifies to host large-scale compute workloads requiring utility-grade infrastructure and environmental standards.

New Albany has become the largest concentration of hyperscale data center construction in the eastern United States, drawing AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Vantage to the site through AEP Ohio's transmission capacity, Ohio's data center tax exemption, and local incentive agreements. Vantage frames this as its 2 billion dollar entry into the Midwest market. No other facility in Ohio has published capacity figures to this site, making this campus the only measured hyperscale buildout currently mapped in the state.
